about: Pre-registered retrieval queries. The `tier` on each entry is not a label:
run.py re-derives it from the measured lexical overlap between the query's
surviving tokens and the target file, using bin/eve's own tokenisation, and
refuses to run if a committed tier disagrees. Edit a fixture memory and the
suite tells you which query changed tier instead of quietly reporting a
different number under the same name.
tier verbatim     2+ surviving tokens land in the target's title, filename
or tags. The query you type when you remember the memory.
tier paraphrase   1+ token lands somewhere in the file, fewer than 2 in the
high-weight fields. Real mid-task questions live here.
tier disjoint     no surviving token appears anywhere in the target. The
ranker cannot retrieve it at any gate; this tier measures
the ceiling of lexical matching, not a tuning mistake.
tier out-of-scope no memory in the store answers this. Anything returned is
a false positive. Unlike the other three, this tier is a
human claim about the fixture, checked once by reading it.
